post.caption: West Point ring gold flew to space. The class of 1835 got the first West Point class rings. They were signets, cut in reverse to seal letters in wax. Each ring since 1917 has a class crest and a school crest. At graduation it is turned so the school crest faces the heart. Graduates donate old gold rings to be melted into one ingot. A small part, Legacy Gold, is saved for the next melt. So every ring since the class of 2002 holds older gold. In 2025 a locket of Legacy Gold flew to the space station. It flew with an astronaut from that class of 2002.
